observations: Proof wording only: the implementer's proof says cert-publish exits 'within 30 s' of its gate dying. The loop checks `kill -0` once per pass and each pass ends with `sleep 60`, so the measured exit was 57.5-59.0 s after the gate died (5.6 s when the gate died just before a check). The code comment ('the next pass says so') is accurate. TestDispatchCertPublishExitsWhenTheClaimGateDies shortens the sleep, so it does not measure real time.

PR body staleness: the 'Look at first' line still says the move runbook 'does not yet grant tailnet clients access to svc:<hostname>', but README.md:173-179 and :726-733 now give the grant and the tcp:443 port.

Hand edit only, as in rounds 1 and 2: a claims value that uses a JSON tab or newline as a separator, or holds an escaped quote before its last entry, is undercounted, so a pod can take a claim that is already spent.

Self-healing: when the cache holds a certificate later than the Secret's, the publish loop's data PATCH can move the resourceVersion between the gate's GET and its PATCH, so the gate's first PATCH gets 409 and advertising waits 30 s (2 of 10 full runs).

[INFERENCE] kube() calls curl with no --max-time, so an API connection that never answers after the handshake could hold the gate in one pass while `kill -0` still sees it alive. The API server's own request timeout normally bounds this; not exercised.
